mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and acceleration of inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such dual-trigger months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 6-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such dual-trigger months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such episodes.
